Every indicator is scored from -2 to +2. The score depends on whether data was supplied, whether the target was met, how performance changed since last year, and how far performance sits from target.
Target achieved and performance improved: Target achieved and performance improved or held steady
Target achieved with a small decline, or: Target achieved with a small decline, or target missed but performance improved
Target achieved but performance dropped: Target achieved but performance dropped sharply, or target missed and performance flat within 40% of target
An objective can score anywhere from min: An objective can score anywhere from minus its weight to plus its weight, and the whole assessment from -{{max}} to +{{max}}. That range is rescaled onto 0-5 for reporting, so a raw score of zero - no movement at all - sits at 2.50, the floor at 0 and the ceiling at 5.
Because each objective is weighted by ex: Because each objective is weighted by exactly its own maximum, averaging the three objective scores and rescaling the total come to the same number. The headline can never disagree with the three figures beneath it.
Each indicator carries a weight derived: Each indicator carries a weight derived from expert scoring. Within an objective, an indicator contributes its share of that objective weight.
The milestone for each objective carries: The milestone for each objective carries 25% of that objective weight, so it moves the score more than any single indicator.
Raw scores run from -3.7333 to +3.7333. The performance index rescales that onto 0-100 so a single headline number can be compared across years and org units.
The assessment is organised into 3 strat: The assessment is organised into 3 strategic objectives aligned with the Health Sector Medium-Term Development Plan (HSMTDP). Each objective carries its own indicators and one milestone.
Regional and district are different inst: Regional and district are different instruments
The two tools are not the same questionn: The two tools are not the same questionnaire, so the app ships both and picks one from the level being assessed. They also reuse the same indicator codes for different indicators, which is why nothing keyed by code is shared between them.
The district tool drops one Objective 1: The district tool drops one Objective 1 indicator that only applies regionally, so its codes run one behind from that point on. 1.17 is "Doctor to population ratio" regionally but "Physician Assistant to population ratio" in a district.

A period decides whether a year accepts: A period decides whether a year accepts submissions. Closing a year stops new submissions but leaves data entry alone, so work in progress is not lost the moment a deadline passes; locking stops editing too. Neither blocks a reviewer from finishing a review already under way.
A year with no period is open: A year with no period is open
The gate is opted into — creating a peri: The gate is opted into — creating a period for one year leaves every other year alone. That way adding periods to an instance which already holds assessments does not freeze the past ones.
Targets are what each row is scored agai: Targets are what each row is scored against, and they are recorded per year and per tool. Edit them in place, import or export the whole tool as CSV, copy last year as a starting point, or reset a year back to the figures the tool ships with.
A target typed back to the figure the to: A target typed back to the figure the tool ships with stops being an override, so a corrected framework in a later release still reaches that row. Rows whose target is genuinely set locally are marked "varies" and are edited on the assessment itself, not here.
Both are read-only. Org units, roles and: Both are read-only. Org units, roles and authorities belong to DHIS2 and are edited in the Maintenance and Users apps; a second place to change them would be a second place for them to be wrong. What these tabs add is what DHIS2 cannot say from inside itself — how much of the hierarchy has been assessed, and who actually reaches this app and through which role.

Rebinding or clearing one marks it "Custom" and overrides what shipped; the app stores only the difference, so a corrected binding in a later release still reaches rows nobody has touched.
The regional and district tools reuse th: The regional and district tools reuse the same codes for different indicators, so each keeps its own mapping. One saved for a tool can never leak into the other.
